title: Dustin Howes's 7-step checklist for launching and scaling an affiliate program
summary: Dustin Howes walks through his 30+ point checklist for building an affiliate program: research, tech stack decisions, creation, announcement, recruitment, management and reporting. His core argument is that programs fail because they are set up poorly and then ignored, and that good partners need onboarding, assets and ongoing attention to produce revenue.

principles.text: Most affiliate programs fail from poor setup and neglect, not because the product is bad.
principles.quote: most of the time uh it's that I see programs fail because it's set up poorly and it's just ignored

principles.text: Good affiliates don't just show up; you must build an environment and resources that keep them excited.
principles.quote: good Affiliates don't just show up they don't just join the program and make magic happen it is hard work optimizing your program and creating an environment that is inviting to those Partners

principles.text: Start with competitive research: sign up for rival programs and benchmark commissions before setting your own.
principles.quote: go sign up for their programs see what they're doing right see what they're doing wrong how much they are offering in commissions you'll need to stay competitive with these payouts

principles.text: Set commissions by what you can afford to give partners and still profit as a company.
principles.quote: figure out what you can afford to give partners and still profit as a company

principles.text: Polish onboarding before announcing: signup page, welcome emails and assets shape the first impression.
principles.quote: this is why we have to be all squared away before or you make the big announcement and tell the people your program is ready signup page needs to be tidy

principles.text: Treat the affiliate manager as a leader who helps partners succeed, and give top performers VIP attention.
principles.quote: the affiliate manager has to be that leader that helps the troops succeed
